subject: shoebill
title: Shoebills Lay Two Eggs, but Usually Only One Chick Lives

scenes.text: This bird lays two eggs, but usually only one chick survives.
Shoebill parents are careful. They pour water from their bills over the eggs, up to five times a day.
The eggs are laid days apart, so the first chick is bigger.
And it attacks its younger sibling, again and again.
The parents don't step in. The big chick takes the food, and often the life of the other.
The second egg is just a backup. If the first chick lives, the second rarely does.

description:
Shoebills usually lay two eggs, up to five days apart, and cool them with water carried in their bills, sometimes four or five times a day.
Usually only one chick survives: the older one outcompetes or attacks its sibling, and the parents do not intervene.
Why do you think the parents let it happen?
first_comment: Shoebills can stand still for hours waiting for a lungfish. Would you want one as a neighbour?
